turns.prompt: Now add a reverse(str) helper the same way.
turns.final:
Done — all three tests pass.

- `src/str.js:11` — `reverse(s)` returns the string reversed, exported alongside `trim` and `capitalize`.
- `test/str.test.js:18` — covers multi-char, single-char, empty, and an emoji case.

One implementation note: I used `[...s]` rather than the usual `s.split('')`. Spread iterates code points, so `reverse('ab🙂')` gives `'🙂ba'`; `split('')` iterates UTF-16 units and would split the emoji's surrogate pair, producing two orphaned halves and a mojibake character. Same cost, strictly fewer ways to be wrong — the emoji assertion in the test locks that in.

It still doesn't handle grapheme clusters: a combining mark (`'e\u0301'`, rendered `é`) detaches from its base letter and reattaches to whatever lands next. Correct handling needs `Intl.Segmenter`, which is a different shape of function than the rest of this module. Worth adding only if you expect that input — say so and I'll do it.

Consistent with the other two helpers, `reverse(null)` throws. No commits made.

turns.final:
Done — all four tests pass.

- `src/str.js:15` — `countWords(s)` counts runs of non-whitespace via `match(/\S+/g)`.
- `test/str.test.js:25` — multi-word, single word, padded, tab/newline separators, empty, whitespace-only.

A word here means "a whitespace-delimited run of non-whitespace," which is the usual reading but has one visible consequence: `countWords('hello -- world')` returns 3, since `--` is its own token. Filtering to tokens containing at least one letter or digit is a one-line change if that matters to you.

I avoided `split(/\s+/)`, the more common spelling, because it returns `['']` on an empty string and so reports 1 word for `''` unless you special-case it. `match` returns `null` there, which `|| []` turns into 0 — no special case, and the empty and whitespace-only assertions pin it.

`countWords(null)` throws, consistent with the other three. No commits made.
